items.description: The words “case report” should be in the title along with the area of focus
2 to 5 key words that identify areas covered in this case report

(a) Introduction – What does this case report add?
(b) Case presentation – What happened during this case?
(c) Conclusion – What did you learn from this case?
One or two sentences summarizing why this case report is important

(a) De-identified patient information
(b) Primary concerns and symptoms of the patient
(c) Medical, family, and psychosocial history
Describe the relevant physical examination (PE) and other significant clinical findings
Historical and current information from this episode of care organized as a timeline

(a) Diagnostic methods (e.g., PE, laboratory testing, imaging)
(b) Diagnostic challenges (e.g., financial, linguistic)
(c) Diagnostic reasoning including other diagnoses considered
(d) Prognostic characteristics (e.g., staging) where applicable

(a) Types of intervention (e.g., pharmacologic, surgical, preventive)
(b) Administration of intervention (e.g., dosage, strength, duration)
(c) Changes in intervention (with rationale)

(a) Clinician and patient-assessed outcomes
(b) Important follow-up diagnostic and other test results
(c) Intervention adherence and tolerability (and how this was assessed)
(d) Adverse and unanticipated events

(a) Strengths and limitations in your approach to this case
(b) Discussion of the relevant medical literature
(c) The rationale for your conclusions
(d) The primary “take-away” lessons from this case report
The patient should share their perspective on the treatment(s) they received
The patient gave their informed consent
